description: Verify CDK synth and deploy the stack to AWS, capturing outputs. Depends on FEAT-101 (frontend dist must exist for CDK BucketDeployment). Network is OPEN_INTERNET; AWS creds valid (account 051826704233, role dasada-kiro, region us-east-1). Run cdk synth, then cdk bootstrap (idempotent) and cdk deploy, and record CloudFrontUrl / ApiUrl / BucketName / TableName from stack Outputs. If deploy succeeds but a later runtime chat/battle call fails with Bedrock AccessDenied, that is an environmental blocker (model access not enabled) to record, NOT a code failure, provided the IAM/model-ID wiring in infra/lib/digital-monster-stack.ts is correct.
steps: cd /projects/sandbox/kiro-digitalmonster/infra && npx cdk synth 2>&1 | tail -40. Confirm synth succeeds and emits the stack template. Fix any synth-time TypeScript/CDK errors (e.g. missing dist, context wiring) and re-run.
Run `npx cdk bootstrap` in infra/ (idempotent; sets up the CDK toolkit stack in account 051826704233 / us-east-1). Capture output.
Run `npx cdk deploy --all --require-approval never` in infra/. Capture the full Outputs block.
Record CloudFrontUrl, ApiUrl, BucketName, TableName into the feature `findings` field verbatim.

Smoke-test the API with curl: GET <ApiUrl>/monster/<random-uuid> should return 404 JSON (monster not found). POST a hatchling then GET it. Record results. If POST /chat or POST /battle returns a Bedrock AccessDenied, record the exact error and note model-access-not-enabled as an environmental blocker.

Do not commit infra changes unless a code fix was required to make synth/deploy pass; if a fix was needed, commit it on branch `fix/cdk-deploy` (one commit). Record all outputs in findings regardless.
acceptance_criteria: `npx cdk deploy` completes and the stack Outputs (CloudFrontUrl, ApiUrl, BucketName, TableName) are captured verbatim in the feature findings
GET <ApiUrl>/monster/<uuid> returns a 404 JSON response (API reachable); hatch+load round-trip recorded

Any Bedrock AccessDenied at runtime is captured with exact error text and labeled an environmental blocker, with confirmation that the IAM policy in digital-monster-stack.ts scopes bedrock:InvokeModel to the chat Lambda on the 3 Claude ARNs
verification: npx cdk deploy --all --require-approval never  # outputs captured

findings.summary: cdk synth + bootstrap + deploy all succeeded on branch fix/frontend-build-ts6310. No code change was required to make synth/deploy pass, so no fix/cdk-deploy commit was created. Core API (getMonster/saveMonster/battle) verified end-to-end. Bedrock chat is blocked by an ENVIRONMENTAL issue (the hard-coded Claude model versions are retired by AWS), not AccessDenied and not a code bug; IAM/model-ID wiring confirmed correct.
findings.cdk_synth: npx cdk synth in infra/ exited 0; template Outputs ApiUrl/CloudFrontUrl/BucketName/TableName emitted.
findings.cdk_bootstrap: npx cdk bootstrap exited 0. Environment aws://051826704233/us-east-1 bootstrapped (CDKToolkit stack UPDATE_COMPLETE, existing toolkit updated).
findings.cdk_deploy: npx cdk deploy --all --require-approval never exited 0. DigitalMonsterStack CREATE_COMPLETE in ~217s (41/41 resources). Stack ARN: arn:aws:cloudformation:us-east-1:051826704233:stack/DigitalMonsterStack/89e39510-c00c-11f1-92b2-12a4cc6ca915

smoke_tests.get_nonexistent_404: GET /monster/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 -> HTTP 404, body {"error":"Monster not found"} (API reachable, 404 JSON as required).
smoke_tests.hatch_roundtrip: POST /monster with a valid baby hatchling (id 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555, name テストっち) -> HTTP 200 {"ok":true,"monster":{...}}. GET /monster/11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 -> HTTP 200 returned the same monster (round-trip confirmed, DynamoDB persistence working).
smoke_tests.battle: POST /battle {"monsterId":"11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555","seed":42} -> HTTP 200. Full battle log returned, winner=player, 5 turns, monster persisted with updated stats. NOTE: /battle takes {monsterId} (loads monster + builds a stage-scaled enemy server-side); it does NOT accept player/enemy objects.
smoke_tests.chat_saved_baby: POST /chat for the saved baby monster -> HTTP 200 {"reply":"…！（まだ言葉を話せないみたい。もっと育ててあげよう！）","modelId":"none"}. Baby stage intentionally returns a canned non-verbal reply WITHOUT invoking Bedrock (the persisted monster is the source of truth for stage, so a client cannot spoof a higher tier for a saved monster).
smoke_tests.chat_bedrock_rookie_haiku: POST /chat with an UNSAVED monsterId at stageId=rookie (falls back to client stage, forcing a real Bedrock InvokeModel on Haiku) -> HTTP 502.

bedrock_blocker.classification: ENVIRONMENTAL (model lifecycle), NOT a code bug and NOT AccessDenied.
bedrock_blocker.exact_error: Bedrock chat failed: This model version has reached the end of its life. Please refer to the AWS documentation for more details.
bedrock_blocker.tiers_affected: All three tiers return the identical end-of-life error: rookie/haiku (anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0), champion/sonnet (anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0), ultimate/opus (anthropic.claude-3-opus-20240229-v1:0).
bedrock_blocker.why_not_accessdenied: The request reached Bedrock and Bedrock reported a model-lifecycle status (end-of-life). There was no AccessDenied / unauthorized error, which means the IAM InvokeModel grant is working.
bedrock_blocker.iam_wiring_confirmed: Verified the DEPLOYED chat Lambda role (DigitalMonsterStack-ChatFnServiceRoleC3825F1B-amoJhNKFcKLZ) inline policy allows ONLY bedrock:InvokeModel on exactly the 3 Claude foundation-model ARNs: arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0, .../anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0, .../anthropic.claude-3-opus-20240229-v1:0. Only the chat Lambda (not getMonster/saveMonster/battle) has any bedrock permission. Matches infra/lib/digital-monster-stack.ts DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS and packages/shared/src/bedrock-models.ts BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS.
bedrock_blocker.remediation_note: Not fixed here (out of scope: this feature verifies deploy). The model IDs are overridable at deploy time via BEDROCK_MODEL_HAIKU/SONNET/OPUS env vars (passed through from stack props bedrockModelHaiku/Sonnet/Opus) or by updating the defaults in both bedrock-models.ts and digital-monster-stack.ts to current (non-retired) Claude model IDs / inference-profile ARNs. Enabling model access alone will not resolve the end-of-life error.

findings.deployed_state: Stack left DEPLOYED (not destroyed) so the next feature (Playwright E2E) can test against CloudFrontUrl https://dctfcixprjknt.cloudfront.net. A test monster (id 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555) exists in the table from smoke tests.
